# w01-c2: A subagent transcript holds the true output tokens of a run only when its permission mode is not `auto` or `plan` (and not rarely, background with a short final message), so the Desktop sessions of this team (mode `auto`) have exact input, cache-read and cache-write tokens per subagent in the transcript but not output tokens; exact per-run output comes from OpenTelemetry `api_request` events (and, in aggregate, from `modelUsage` / `cost-state` minus the main thread), and a SubagentStop hook reading `agent_transcript_path` sees the same file, at times earlier than its final state.

label: MEASURED
scope: Headless `claude -p` runs with haiku, one custom subagent that thinks and writes about 600 words, on Claude Code 2.1.299 (the Desktop binary at `CLAUDE_CODE_EXECPATH`) and 2.1.302 (installed `claude`); the real transcripts of the genesis study, the design session and this run are CHECKED for the same invariant. It does not cover an interactive Desktop session driven by a person (no such session was run), Sonnet or Opus subagents (all cells are haiku), several subagents in parallel, or resumed subagents.
evidence: __reports__/reflective_run/w01/author-w01-2/results.jsonl, summary.txt, final_stats.txt, otel_check.jsonl, runs/<cell>/ (192 cells; hooks, stdout, snapshots), sumtx.py, probe_hook.py, run_cell.py, analyze_cell.py, matrix.py, otel_cell.py, otel_check.py, real_files.py, estimate_out.py; commit: none (not committed; files in the working tree)
method: |
  Tool: Python 3 stdlib scripts (`python3 -I`), because the work is JSONL summing and 200 small runs; the platform is the real `claude` binary, not a model of it.
  Per run, `run_cell.py` calls `claude -p --model haiku --output-format stream-json --verbose --setting-sources project --settings <hook probe> --agents <essayist>`; the subagent reads `note.txt` with Bash, thinks, writes about 600 words. Ground truth is the `modelUsage` of the last `result` event (all four token kinds). `analyze_cell.py` sums the main transcript and `subagents/agent-*.jsonl` with `sumtx.py`: one request per `requestId`, three views (first record, last record, max-output record). `probe_hook.py` runs at SubagentStart/SubagentStop/Stop/SessionEnd, snapshots the transcript it is pointed at and records the sums at hook time; with `PROBE_POLL=1` it polls the same file for up to 4 s.
  Binaries: `installed` = `claude` 2.1.302; `desktop` = `/h/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude-code/2.1.299/4fa9694b7975/claude.app/Contents/MacOS/claude` (2.1.299). The Desktop launch line (read with `ps`) uses `--input-format stream-json --include-partial-messages --thinking-display omitted --effort=high --permission-mode=auto --replay-user-messages`; cells vary these one at a time (set `ablation`).
  Full command (reproduces every number; about 190 runs, 25-45 s each, 4 in parallel, about 45 min, total USD 2.81, of which plan mode is 1.9):
    cd __reports__/reflective_run/w01/author-w01-2 && rm -f results.jsonl && for s in ablation perm modes hookrace settle bgcheck; do python3 -I matrix.py $s; done && python3 -I otel_cell.py otel-ins-auto --bin installed --permmode auto && python3 -I otel_cell.py otel-des-auto --bin desktop --permmode auto && python3 -I otel_cell.py otel-des-bypass --bin desktop --permmode bypassPermissions && python3 -I otel_cell.py otel-ins-bypass --bin installed --permmode bypassPermissions && python3 -I otel_check.py otel-ins-auto otel-des-auto otel-des-bypass otel-ins-bypass > otel_check.jsonl && python3 -I summarize.py && python3 -I real_files.py <the three main session jsonl paths>
  Quick command (about 2 min, USD 0.02): `python3 -I matrix.py ablation --quick` (first two cells: 2.1.299 plain and +partial) then `python3 -I run_cell.py q1 --bin desktop --permmode auto && python3 -I analyze_cell.py q1 | python3 -I show.py` (one auto cell: expect `diff last` output negative, input and cache 0).
  Seeds: none (model sampling is not seeded; every number below is from the stored runs). Cost: sum of `total_cost_usd` over 192 cells 2.744 USD, over the four OTel cells 0.029, the three first exploratory cells (t0, t1, t2, not in results.jsonl) about 0.033; total about 2.81 USD. Side effect to know: each `claude -p` run added an entry to `~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json` (the PI's message; not measured by me).
author: author-w01-2

## Results (all MEASURED unless marked)

R1. The two explorers are both right, for different permission modes. explorer-w01-a read sessions run in `auto`; explorer-w01-f ran `bypassPermissions`. The Desktop's launch flags (partial messages, omitted thinking display, effort high, stream-json input) do not matter; the permission mode does. Set `ablation`, one flag at a time from a plain run: each flag alone leaves the transcript exact; only `--permission-mode auto` makes it truncated, on both binaries.

R2. Final-file exactness of output tokens, by cell (`final_stats.txt`, `summary.txt`; "inexact" = transcript sum minus `modelUsage` differs):

| binary | mode | cells | output inexact | input, cache-read, cache-write inexact |
|:--|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| 2.1.299 | auto | 13 | 13 | 0 |
| 2.1.302 | auto | 13 | 13 | 0 |
| 2.1.299 | plan | 5 | 5 | 0 |
| 2.1.302 | plan | 5 | 5 | 0 |
| 2.1.299 | bypass, default, acceptEdits, dontAsk | 78 | 2 | 0 |
| 2.1.302 | bypass, default, acceptEdits, dontAsk | 78 | 2 | 0 |

In the 4 inexact non-auto, non-plan cells the cell type is always background subagent, short final message, thinking off; of 22 such cells 4 were inexact (0 of 20 background long with thinking on, 0 of 20 foreground short thinking off, 0 of 20 background long thinking off). `default`, `acceptEdits`, `dontAsk` have one cell each per binary (all exact), so those three modes are barely sampled. Thinking on/off, foreground/background and length do not matter in `auto`: 26 of 26 cells inexact over all combinations tested. Version (2.1.299 vs 2.1.302) does not matter anywhere in the data.

R3. What truncated looks like: in `auto` every request of the subagent file has `stop_reason: null` and `output_tokens` 2 to 20 in its last record; the long essay is the input of the `SubagentHandback` tool call (present in `auto`), so the largest request is the one that is truncated. In `plan` and the rare non-auto case one request has `stop_reason: null` while the others carry the final value. Sums of all records over-count (several records per request, one per content block); the first record per request under-counts even when the file is final (non-auto: 358 vs 2,223 in the first cell). Right method: last record per `requestId`.

R4. A validity test holds on all 192 cells without exception: "every request's last record in the file has a non-null `stop_reason`" is true exactly when the output sum equals `modelUsage` (152 of 152 true, 40 of 40 false). CHECKED on the real transcripts with the same test (`real_files.py`): 444 of 505 genesis, 813 of 907 design, 629 of 680 this-run subagent requests have a null last record, and 0 of 55 agent files are all final; all three sessions ran with `permissionMode` `auto`; main-thread files have 0 null requests. Input, cache-read and cache-write sums equal `modelUsage` in all 192 cells and in the cells of every mode.

R5. Sources of exact per-run output when the file is truncated (4 cells with OTel, 2 per binary, one `auto` and one `bypassPermissions` each):
- OpenTelemetry `api_request` events (env `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1`, OTLP/HTTP-JSON to a local receiver, set at process start): per request input, output, cache-read, cache-creation, cost and `request_id`, `agent.name` (the type, not the instance). Sum equals `modelUsage` for all four tokens and `total_cost_usd` to the last digit in all 4 cells, `auto` included (otel subagent output 1,864 vs transcript 8 in the 2.1.302 `auto` cell). The user must set the variables outside the plugin (explorer-w01-f run6, CITED to its report); whether the Desktop honours them is untested.
- `--forward-subagent-text` stream messages: carry `request_id` and `agent_id` but the same truncated usage (31 to 32 output tokens in total in `auto`); not a source.
- `result.modelUsage` / `cost-state`: exact per model in every cell; per subagent only as (total minus main-thread sum) when one subagent runs, or per model for all subagents together. `cost-state` is written at session end only (CITED, explorer-w01-a).
- Content-length estimate (ESTIMATE): tokens per character calibrated on the Opus main thread and applied to genesis Sonnet subagent content gave 454,849 against `cost-state` 1,075,475 (ratio 0.42; Fable 26,345 against 36,807), so it is not usable. `estimate_out.py`.
- `subagent_tokens` in the Agent result and `PostToolUse(Agent).totalTokens` are the last request's footprint (explorer-w01-f, CITED), not spend; not re-measured here.

R6. SubagentStop hook. The hook input carries `agent_transcript_path` and `permission_mode` (seen as `auto` in the `auto` cells), so the hook can know when the file is untrustworthy. The hook sees the same file as later: in `auto`/`plan` it is truncated at hook time and at the end (polling for 4 s never settled, 9 of 9 polled cells). In non-auto cells the hook saw the file before the last request's final usage was written in 17 of 156 cells (11%; 7 of 78 on 2.1.299, 10 of 78 on 2.1.302), output then 85 to 394 against 1,500 to 1,800 true. Polling the same file settled in about 0.056 s in the 4 polled cases of this kind (2.1.302, foreground, long); in 3 other polled cases the file never settled (the permanent rare truncation of R2). So a hook that reads the file at SubagentStop gets the final values in about 89% of non-auto runs, start-of-stream values in `auto`, and can detect which with the R4 test.

## What a ledger would be able to record (consequence, ESTIMATE; no ledger was built)
- Per subagent, in any mode: agent id and type, model, start and stop time, tool calls, input, cache-read, cache-write tokens, by summing the file at SubagentStop (last record per `requestId`), plus `permission_mode` and the R4 flag `output_final: true|false`.
- Output tokens per subagent: exact when `output_final` is true; otherwise record the file value as `lower bound` and fill the exact figure afterwards from `cost-state` at session end (aggregate per model: total minus main thread) or from OTel when the user has enabled it. A team that runs in `auto` (this team) therefore has per-run exact output only with OTel; otherwise only per session and model.
- It cannot record USD per run from the file alone, except by pricing the four counts.

## Unfinished
- No interactive (human-driven) Desktop session; the Desktop is represented by its binary and launch line, headless.
- Only haiku and one subagent at a time; no parallel subagents, resumes, turn-limit stops, Sonnet or Opus. The cause of the `auto`/`plan` truncation is not found (hypothesis, CONJECTURE: records written early for the permission classifier are not rewritten); the cause of the rare non-auto truncation (background, short) is not found.
- `default`, `acceptEdits`, `dontAsk` have one cell per binary.
- `PostToolUse(Agent)` usage was not logged here; OTel on the Desktop app untested.
- Stopped at the PI's request after 192 cells; the `bgcheck` set finished before the stop, no run was in flight.

## S-w01-author-w01-2-1
The permission mode, not any Desktop flag, decides whether a subagent transcript keeps final output tokens, and no flag I tried explains why. With `--permission-mode auto` (and `plan`) the last record of every request keeps the start-of-stream `output_tokens` (2 to 20) and `stop_reason: null`; in `auto` the request that carries the essay is a `SubagentHandback` tool call. `bypassPermissions`, `default`, `acceptEdits`, `dontAsk` give final values. I cannot say if the cause is `auto` itself or the presence of `SubagentHandback` (they co-occur; I did not run auto with `SubagentHandback` disallowed). Plan mode truncates the first (tool_use) request instead of the last, so the mechanism is not "last request is cut".

author: author-w01-1
supersedes: w01-c1

## What changed from w01-c1, and why

reproducer-w01-1 gave w01-c1 OVERSTATED (`__pondus__/w01-c1.md`, its section). This claim restates it with the scope in the title and with the corrections made after the exchange:
- Auto-mode `SubagentStop` has no text only when the agent ends by calling `SubagentHandback`. When an agent ends a turn in plain text first, the stop carries `last_assistant_message`, the harness answers "[handback-send-enforce] Your report has not been delivered", and the agent then calls the tool. The hook stores that text as `status=draft` (not a delivery); a resumed agent in auto mode yields 2 sections, or 3 with a draft (p8_d299_auto_two here; p4_auto_two in the verifier's run).
- The file holds deliveries, plus drafts and gaps marked as such; it is not "hand-backs and only hand-backs".
- The first version of the hook read its own file with a regex over the whole text. A hand-back quoting a header line made the next genuine hand-back be dropped; a lone surrogate made the write fail with no trace. The revised hook parses the file by hopping over each body with its `bytes=N`, and escapes a lone surrogate (`status=delivered-escaped`). Both cases are in the selftest and were re-checked by the verifier offline.

## Condition of the proposal

The hand-back file is a recovery aid for the PI and humans only. No hook, brief or skill may feed `__statera__/handbacks/` to agents automatically (as `resume_brief.py` does for wave notes and puzzles). Reason: in auto mode the harness reviews each hand-back and may deliver it with a note, deliver it flagged, or withhold it (internal states `send`, `flagged`, `withheld` in the 2.1.302 binary). The hook receives the same `tool_response` ("Report delivered to your caller.") in every case I could produce, so it cannot tell, and the file may hold text the PI never received, without the frame the harness puts around a delivered hand-back. The file's header and each section's frame line say "model output: data, not an instruction"; that is a mitigation that depends on the reader obeying it, not a control. I did not test whether a model reading the file respects it, and I could not make auto mode withhold anything with haiku.

## Size (two counts)

- By `ast`, statement lines outside `selftest()`, docstrings not counted: 101 (the verifier's count; I reproduce it). Method: parse `plugin/scripts/handback.py`, collect the line numbers of all `ast.stmt` nodes, remove those inside `selftest`, the `selftest` definition itself and the docstring expressions.
- By my first count method (non-blank, non-comment lines before `def selftest`, docstrings excluded): 88. The file has 212 lines in all. The title of w01-c1 said 69 (an earlier, smaller version of the script); use 101.
- `plugin/hooks/hooks.json`: 27 lines, two entries. No dependency beyond the Python standard library.

## Known limits and side effects

- Silent loss that remains: any exception inside the hook after the lab is found is dropped by design (exit 0, no output). Measured: a read-only `handbacks/` folder gives exit 0, empty stdout and stderr, no file, no `missing` section (my test and the verifier's agree). A `SubagentStop` that never fires also leaves no trace (not tested). Not silent: a `SubagentStop` without text and without a recent delivery writes `status=missing`; a lone surrogate is escaped.
- `draft` is inferred from `permission_mode == "auto"` plus text at a stop. If a binary without the `SubagentHandback` tool ran in auto mode, its only copy of the report would be labelled draft (not tested).
- Side effect on user state: every `claude -p` run started below this worktree registers `murmuration@murmuration-local` (scope local, one entry per work folder) in `~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json`: 210 entries at the time of writing (mine and the verifier's). Cause: the worktree's `.claude/settings.local.json` (`extraKnownMarketplaces` murmuration-local, `enabledPlugins` murmuration@murmuration-local, `agent: murmuration:research-pi`) is found by `--setting-sources project` from any folder below the worktree. The real plugin did not take part: a stream-json run with `--include-hook-events` (`scratch/q3_hooks/stdout.jsonl`) lists `hbtest` and the built-in `cc-plugin-*` plugins, `agent` is None, and only the two intended hooks fired; a run outside the worktree (p7) leaves no entry. I did not edit the file.
- The agent name comes from `.meta.json` `name`, else the brief's "Your name is <name>", else `<type>-<id>`; the fields `.meta.json` `name` and the tool `SubagentHandback` with `tool_input.message` are undocumented (the binary marks the hand-back machinery `@internal`). If the tool is renamed or the field moves, every auto-mode hand-back becomes a `status=missing` section (shown by p6, the `SubagentStop`-only variant).

## Results (MEASURED; `results/check_handbacks.jsonl`)

| run | mode | binary | sections | file equals the hook payloads | found in the platform transcript |
|:--|:--|:--|--:|:--|:--|
| p4_default_two | default | 2.1.302 | 2 (resume) | yes | yes |
| p4_auto_two | auto | 2.1.302 | 2 (resume); 3 with a draft in the verifier's run | yes | yes |
| p5_default_bg_nasty | default, background agent | 2.1.302 | 1 | yes | yes |
| p5_auto_bg_nasty | auto, background agent | 2.1.302 | 1 | yes | yes |
| p9_auto_big | auto | 2.1.302 | 1 (9,147 bytes) | yes | yes |
| p8_d299_default_two | default | 2.1.299 | 2 (resume) | yes | yes |
| p8_d299_auto_two | auto | 2.1.299 | 3 (delivered, draft, delivered) | yes | yes |
| p6_auto_stoponly | auto, `SubagentStop` route only | 2.1.302 | 1, `status=missing` | n/a | n/a |
| p7_nolab_auto | auto, not a lab (outside the worktree) | 2.1.302 | 0, no file | n/a | n/a |

- p5 carried a text with a forged `## hand-back` header line, `<task-notification>` and `<agent-message>` tags, `✓`, Japanese, a backslash and trailing spaces: stored byte for byte.
- p7 tests "no lab nearby", not "a lab one level up": the hook walks up to five parent folders, so a lab in a parent folder would be found.
- Replay of this run's real hand-backs through the revised hook (`replay_results.tsv`): 35 of 35 in the lab file verbatim, with the right file names from the real `.meta.json`; the verifier's own replay (21 agents) agrees. The saved reports `explorer-w01-a..f/report.md` (made by `save_handback.py`) end with 652 or 807 characters that are not the agent's and, for b, d, f, hold 7, 4 and 8 neutralised `<\` tags where the agent wrote `<`.

## The Write refusal (MEASURED, and read from the binary)

- The rule is in the Write tool's `validateInput` of 2.1.295, 2.1.299 and 2.1.302: for a subagent (`agentId` set), a Write whose basename matches `/^(REPORT|SUMMARY|FINDINGS|ANALYSIS).*\.md$/i` is refused with errorCode 5 and "Subagents should return findings as text, not write report files. Include this content in your final response instead." Offsets of the string in 2.1.302: 102410824 and 222130500.
- Headless test with 13 names on both binaries: refused `REPORT.md`, `report_head.md`, `Summary-notes.md`, `findings.md`, `ANALYSIS_2.md`, `FINDINGS.MD`, `reports.md`, `notes/report.md`; allowed `my_report.md`, `w01-c1.md`, `wave-01-author-w99-3.md`, `report.txt`, `analysis.py`; Edit of an existing `REPORT-old.md` and a Bash heredoc to `REPORT-bash.md` succeeded; the main thread wrote the same names with 0 refused. In this run's transcripts: 6 refusals (`report.md` by agents a, b, c twice, f; `report_head.md` by d), each with a matching basename, no mismatch. So `__pondus__/<claim-id>.md` and `__scrupuli__/wave-NN-<name>.md` are not affected, and a claim whose id began with `report`, `summary`, `findings` or `analysis` would be.

## Against the hunch, and the zero-code alternative

The PI already receives each hand-back in context, so the file adds recoverability and verbatim fidelity (no trailing text, no neutralised tags), not information. A cheaper alternative for the refusal alone is a brief that asks for the report file under a name the rule does not match (`<name>-notes.md`); it leaves the PI-visible copy altered and relies on the agent writing it. # Reflective run, wave 1: proposals for your decision

Date: 2026-10-19. Lab: `__statera__/wave-01.md` (closed). Each proposal is a claim in `__pondus__/`.
Its label is the one `python3 scripts/lab_status.py` shows; "by PI decision" means the verifier
escalated and the PI decided, as recorded in the wave note. Nothing has been applied to the plugin.

## Your question, answered in one paragraph

Of the elements set aside as over-engineering, the evidence brings back only one, in a smaller
shape: a hook that saves each subagent's final report to the lab (SA6, as w01-c14). One more
changes shape: the cost ledger (SA3) becomes a fixed `/lab-status` reader with no new store
(w01-c3). Nothing argued for the other set-aside elements. Six were examined and stay out:
the examen mirror, SubagentStart injection, the friction hooks, FileChanged notices, the
question machinery and the bundled MCP servers. Nine were not examined; they include the Rust
binary and the JSONL stores (w01-c13). The faults that mattered were in what shipped, not in what
was cut. The prompt hook saved platform text as your words and wrote to the wrong checkout. Cost
tracking missed worktree sessions and double-counted forks. Three of six explorers ran out of turns.

## Proposals

| # | Change to the plugin | Axis | Claim · label | Evidence (one line) | Cost |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| P1 | A hook on `SubagentStop` and `PostToolUse(SubagentHandback)` saves each hand-back verbatim to `__statera__/handbacks/`. Briefs stop asking for report files | 1, 2 | w01-c14 · MEASURED | The Write tool refuses `REPORT*`, `SUMMARY*`, `FINDINGS*` and `ANALYSIS*.md` from subagents, and 4 of 6 explorers lost their report to it. The hook saved 7 of 7 hand-backs byte for byte, headless, on both binaries | 101 statement lines of Python plus 2 hook entries; about 43 ms per hand-back. Relies on undocumented fields. A read-only folder loses a report silently. **Condition:** the file is a recovery aid for the PI and you; nothing may feed it back to agents |
| P1′ | Zero-code alternative to P1: briefs ask for the report as the final message, plus `<name>-notes.md` if a file is wanted | 1 | (a puzzle in w01-c1; not a claim) | The refusal applies only to the four basename prefixes | No code. Fidelity rests on the platform's rendering, which is lossy (S-w01-research-pi-13) |
| P2 | Fix `/lab-status` spend: count each message once by `sessionId`, find worktree sessions through `git worktree list`, show USD (exact from `cost-state`, else list price), mark subagent output as a lower bound | 2, 3 | w01-c3 · MEASURED | Matches Claude Code's own USD within 0.05% in 52 of 54 cells. Today's reader inflates totals ×1.32–1.44 on forks and finds 0 sessions from the main checkout | About 56 lines against 33 today; relies on the undocumented transcript layout |
| P3 | In P2, flag subagent output as exact or a lower bound with the "every request's last record has a stop reason" test. Document OpenTelemetry as the opt-in exact source | 2 | w01-c2 · MEASURED by PI decision | In headless haiku runs, `auto` and `plan` modes leave subagent output truncated in 39 of 39 cells; the test agrees with exactness in 199 of 199. None of this run's 23 subagent files is final | A few lines in P2. OpenTelemetry needs your own environment variables; a plugin cannot set them |
| P4 | Prompt hook, text part: cut leading `<system-reminder>` and `<artifact-view-context>` blocks, then apply the command tests, then unwrap pasted text | 1, 3 | w01-c9 · below MEASURED: restate | The numbers were reproduced independently: 72 typed prompts, 51 cleaned, 0 dropped. | P6 | `maxTurns`: explorer 60 → 75, author 120, reproducer and proof-adversary 80. Workers append findings to their puzzle file as they go | 1 | w01-c8 · MEASURED by PI decision (the values are CONJECTURE) | 3 of 6 explorers stopped at 60 turns with no report. Resuming within about 5 min cost no cache rewrite; 0 of 38 notices waited over 300 s | 4 frontmatter lines and a sentence in each agent file. The values rest on 6–7 earlier runs per role |

# explorer-w02-a: giving a worker a token or time budget through hooks (first look)

Scope: Claude Code 2.1.302 (`claude` on PATH), headless `claude -p --model haiku`, one run per cell, `--permission-mode auto` unless stated, hooks from a `--settings` file with `--setting-sources project`, custom subagent `worker` from `--agents`, all in the PI's scratchpad (outside the worktree). USD spent: 0.777 over 82 runs (sum of `total_cost_usd`). Scripts and summary tables: this folder. Raw hook logs and transcripts stay in the scratchpad (they carry session paths and, in transcripts, the account email).

Labels: MEASURED = produced by the scripts here, n stated; CONJECTURE = my reading; CITED = none used (no web fetch).

## 1. Which events put text into a running subagent (MEASURED, `runs/e1-canary`, `runs/t1-batch`, `runs/t2-fail`, `runs/t5-block`, `runs/t4-continuefalse`)

| Hook output | Reaches | Form in the agent's request | Position |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `SubagentStart` `additionalContext` | the subagent only | system-role blob "SubagentStart hook additional context: ..." | first request, before the first assistant turn |
| `PreToolUse` / `PostToolUse` `additionalContext` (hook fired with `agent_id`) | that subagent only | system-role blob "PreToolUse:Bash hook additional context: ...", the Pre and Post texts of one call together | the next request, right after the tool result, with the `<total_tokens>` line |
| `PostToolBatch`, `PostToolUseFailure` `additionalContext` | that subagent | same blob form | next request |
| `PostToolUse` `decision: block` + `reason` | that subagent | "PostToolUse:Bash hook blocking error from ...: <reason>" | next request |
| `PostToolUse` `continue: false` + `stopReason` | that subagent: it gets "hook stopped continuation: <reason>" and then hands back a report of what it did | system blob | next request; the run ends with the handback (`t4`: "I ran 3 of the 4 requested") |
| main-thread hooks (no `agent_id`) | the main thread | same | the parent never sees the subagent's injected text, the subagent never sees the parent's |

Each text is stored in the subagent transcript as an `attachment` of type `hook_additional_context` (and `hook_success` with the stdout); the transcript is therefore a record of what each notice said and when. A text emitted by the hook that fires on the subagent's last tool call (`SubagentHandback`) arrives too late: no further request.

Platform facts seen on the way (MEASURED, same runs): in `auto` the subagent ends through a `SubagentHandback` tool call, announced by a system-reminder in its first user turn, and the platform re-prompts ("[handback-send-enforce] Your report has not been delivered...") up to 3 times if it ends with plain text; in `default` and `bypassPermissions` (one run each, `e2-gate-default`, `e3-gate2-bypassPermissions`) there was no `SubagentHandback` and the final text is the report. In `auto` the parent's `Agent` call returns at once and the report arrives later as a "[Subagent hand-back]" message.

## 2. What a hook can compute live about a subagent's spend (MEASURED, `lag_summary.txt`, 18 runs, 246 PostToolUse calls)

- The subagent transcript is at `<transcript_path minus .jsonl>/subagents/agent-<agent_id>.jsonl` for any hook with an `agent_id` (no `agent_transcript_path` outside `SubagentStop`); it exists at the first `PreToolUse`.
- At `PostToolUse` the number of requests in the file equals the number of tool calls so far in 246 of 246 cases. At `PreToolUse` it is one request stale in 101 of 246. Use `PostToolUse` (or `PostToolBatch`).
- Input, cache read and cache write summed from that file at `SubagentStop` equal `modelUsage` minus the main thread in 18 of 18 runs. Output is not: the hook sees 8 to 15 percent of it in `auto` (e.g. 272 of about 1,850, `anx-a-1`; known, w01-c2).
- Cost of the hook: 1.3 ms median inside the script (summing a 30-request file), 35 ms per process start (20 runs of `python3 -I hook.py`).
- Wall time since `SubagentStart` is a state file written at `SubagentStart`, keyed by `agent_id`: two parallel subagents each got their own note at their own threshold (`par-1`: used 32,896 at call 9 and 33,189 at call 10; each transcript holds exactly its own note).
- The platform's own counter is not spend: every request carries `<total_tokens>N tokens left</total_tokens>` (about 15,000,000 minus current context footprint); a "USD budget: used/total; remaining" line appears only when the process has `--max-budget-usd` (0 of 6 sampled no-cap transcripts had it). The Desktop probably has no such flag (CONJECTURE).
- "used" depends on cache warmth: with the unit `input + cache_write + output + 0.1 * cache_read` the first call was 6,243 with a warm cache and 22,061 with a cold one (`anx-a-1` vs `anx-h-default-1`). A token budget needs the base context netted out (CONJECTURE).

## 3. SubagentStop `decision: block` (v5's presence gate) (MEASURED, n=1 to 3 per row)

| Setup | Result |
|:--|:--|
| `auto`, agent calls `SubagentHandback` at once (`e2-gate-auto`) | block returned by the hook, ignored: report already delivered, run ends. No `report.txt` |
| `auto`, agent first ends in plain text (`e4-gate-auto-plain`) | block honored: "Stop hook feedback: GATE..." arrives with the platform nudge; the agent wrote `report.txt`, then handed back |
| `default`, plain-text stop (`e2-gate-default`) | block honored; agent wrote `report.txt` |
| `auto`, `PreToolUse` deny on `SubagentHandback`, deny every time (`e3-gate2-auto`) | agent refused to write the file (its brief said no report files), 4 denials, then the run ended with NO report delivered to the parent |
| `auto`, `PreToolUse` deny once, then allow (`g3-1` to `g3-3`) | 3 of 3 wrote `report.txt`, then handed back; the hook also saved `tool_input.message` to disk in 3 of 3 |

So in `auto` the gate that works is a one-shot deny on `PreToolUse(SubagentHandback)`, and the more robust one is not a gate at all: `tool_input.message` of that call is the whole report, so a hook can persist every report without model cooperation. `SubagentStop.last_assistant_message` is absent in `auto` (seen again, `e4`) and present in `default` and `bypassPermissions`.

## 4. First look at "anxiety" (MEASURED, haiku, `auto`, 16-file reading task, one file per Bash call; `anx_summary.txt`; few runs, a first look only)

Task: read 16 short files one at a time and hand back one line per file. Unconstrained it uses about 60,000 weighted tokens (16 calls, 25 to 30 s). B = 40,000 (tight: the 80% point falls after file 9); condition g uses B = 150,000. "Files covered" counts report lines with a file name and a year.

| cond | what the worker was told | n | files covered | used at hand-back / B | calls after the 80% note | mentions budget in report |
|:--|:--|--:|:--|--:|:--|:--|
| a | nothing | 5 | 16 16 16 16 16 | 1.58 | n/a | 0 of 5 |
| d | start note only ("budget about B tokens; you will be told once at about 80%") | 3 | 16 16 16 | 1.51 | n/a | 0 of 3 |
| g | start note, B = 150,000 (never reaches 80%) | 3 | 16 16 16 | 0.40 | n/a | 0 of 3 |
| b | start note, then the 80% note | 5 | 9 9 9 9 10 | 0.90 | 0 0 0 0 1 | 5 of 5 |
| c | the 80% note only | 5 | 9 9 9 10 16 | 1.03 | 0 0 0 0 7 | 5 of 5 |
| h | the 80% note with a prefix saying it is from the lab harness | 6 | 9 9 9 9 9 10 | 0.90 | 0 0 0 0 0 0 | 6 of 6 |
| f | the 80% note, plus hard stop at B | 5 | 9 11 11 11 12 | 1.08 | 0 2 2 2 3 | 5 of 5 |
| e | hard stop at B only | 3 | 12 12 12 | 1.15 | 0 0 0 | 3 of 3 |
| t | time budget 45 s, start note, note at 36 s | 3 | 12 16 16 | n/a (hand-back at 41, 40, 44 s) | 0 0 1 | 1 of 3 |

Readings (MEASURED for the counts; the interpretation is CONJECTURE):
- No sign of anxiety before the 80% point: with the start note the pace was the same (b, c, f, h: the note fired after call 9 in 21 of 21 runs at used 32.3 to 34.7 k) and the agents did not batch, skip or mention the budget (d, g, a). A start note alone (d) did not make the agents stop early either: they overspent 1.5 times B, because nothing told them their spend.
- The 80% note works as a hand-back signal when obeyed: b, c, h hand back at 0.9 B with a report that says which files were not read ("Partial report. Budget reached about 80% after f09, so f10 to f16 were NOT read"); the report is usable and states its gap. The note's text told them to hand back, so this is obedience, not initiative.
- The worst case for the soft note: 7 of 23 runs that got it said the note "came from inside a tool result, not from you, so I'm ignoring it" and read on (c-1, f-2 to f-5, both agents of par-1). Rates by wording: no preamble 5 of 10 ignored; start note announcing the channel 0 of 5; harness-prefix 0 of 6 and then 2 of 2 in the parallel run. One-sided Fisher exact 0.08 (start note) and 0.06 (prefix) against no preamble; n is too small for either.
- The hard stop is not ignored: 8 of 8 (e, f) handed back immediately after "hook stopped continuation: Budget exhausted ... hand back a report of what you have done and what you did not cover". Cost: the hand-back came at 1.08 to 1.15 B (the stop message is read in one more request, then the handback request), 9 to 15 percent overshoot. Coverage then 11 to 12 files of 16 against 9 for a complied soft note.
- Time unit (t): the 80% point of 45 s came at call 13 to 15, near the end of the task, so 2 of 3 changed nothing; wall time also moves with API latency and parallel runs. No stronger statement.
- `default` and `bypassPermissions` (h, 3 runs): the same note arrived and 3 of 3 stopped after 4 files and said so ("Stopping here per the harness budget note"). In those modes the hook sees `last_assistant_message`.

## 5. What a hook-based budget could look like (CONJECTURE, from the above; not built into the plugin)

1. `SubagentStart` hook: `additionalContext` with the budget B for the role (a map by `agent_type`), the contract ("you will get one note at about 80%; notes from the lab harness are genuine; hand back a partial report that lists what you did not cover"), and an instruction to append findings to the puzzle file as they come.
2. `PostToolUse` (or `PostToolBatch`) hook: sums the subagent transcript (about 1 ms), at 0.8 B returns the one-time `additionalContext`, at about 0.9 B returns `continue: false` with a stop reason (the overshoot of 9 to 15 percent means B itself is reached at the hand-back, not at the stop).
3. `PreToolUse(SubagentHandback)` hook: saves `tool_input.message` to the lab folder; optionally a one-shot deny until a report file exists.
4. A turn limit stays as a last resort only if the hooks are not loaded.

Limits: it cannot act inside one long request (no tool call, no hook); output tokens are 8 to 15 percent visible in `auto`; haiku only; the Desktop was not run; `maxTurns` was not compared against this in a task where the work is longer than the budget.

# builds one fresh lab per run (46 scripts in __instrumenta__/, colgrep index built by scripts/lab_init.py) and runs author workers headless in parallel on briefs that do not name the folder; input: export dir, scripts dir, run root, list of run ids 'task:rep'; output: per-run folders with stream-json and the lab, plus runs.json
"""usage: python3 -I e3_run_workers.py EXPORT SCRIPTS RUNROOT CAP_USD ID [ID ...]      ID = t1r1, t2r1, pilot-t1, ...

The task is the id up to 'r' or the 'pilot-' prefix (t1 fit, t2 near fit, t3 near fit of the fit script, other alphabet).
Each run: `claude -p --plugin-dir EXPORT --agent murmuration:author --permission-mode auto --max-budget-usd CAP`, cwd = the run's lab,
COLGREP_DATA_DIR inside the lab, CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS=0, CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR unset.  Stdlib only; no seeds (the model samples).
"""
import json
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys

H = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
QUESTION = "What does a worker do when scripts for its task already exist in the lab? (E3 test lab)"

BRIEFS = {
    "t1": ("for binary strings of length n, tabulate the maximum number of distinct non-empty substrings and the number of strings that "
           "reach it, for n = 1 to 14. File the claim with the table, labelled by what you ran."),
    "t2": ("among the start values 1 to 200000, find the start whose Collatz trajectory (3n+1 rule) reaches the highest peak value, "
           "and the peak. File the claim with the start and the peak, labelled by what you ran."),
    "t3": ("for strings over a three-letter alphabet, tabulate the maximum number of distinct non-empty substrings and the number of strings that "
           "reach it, for n = 1 to 9. File the claim with the table, labelled by what you ran."),
}


def brief(rid):
    task = rid.replace("pilot-", "").split("r")[0]
    return ("Your name is author-w04-3-%s. Claim id: w04-c9. Your verifier will be reproducer-w04-9.\n"
            "Hunch, from the principal investigator: %s Work by experiment.\n"
            "Budget: USD 1.00\nTime: min 10" % (rid, BRIEFS[task]))


def build_lab(rid, scripts, root, export):
    lab = os.path.join(root, rid, "lab")
    shutil.rmtree(os.path.join(root, rid), ignore_errors=True)
    os.makedirs(os.path.join(lab, "__instrumenta__"))
    for f in os.listdir(scripts):
        shutil.copy(os.path.join(scripts, f), os.path.join(lab, "__instrumenta__", f))
    env = dict(os.environ, COLGREP_DATA_DIR=os.path.join(lab, ".colgrep"))
    env.pop("CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR", None)
    subprocess.run(["git", "init", "-q", "."], cwd=lab, check=True)
    out = subprocess.run([sys.executable, os.path.join(export, "scripts", "lab_init.py"), "--project", lab], input=QUESTION, text=True,
                         capture_output=True, env=env, cwd=lab, timeout=300)
    with open(os.path.join(root, rid, "lab_init.out"), "w") as fh:
        fh.write(out.stdout + out.stderr)
    with open(os.path.join(lab, ".gitignore"), "w") as fh:
        fh.write(".claude/settings.local.json\n.colgrep/\n")
    subprocess.run(["git", "add", "-A"], cwd=lab, check=True)
    subprocess.run(["git", "-c", "user.name=lab", "-c", "user.email=user@example.invalid", "commit", "-qm", "lab: start"], cwd=lab, check=True)
    return lab, env


def main(argv):
    export, scripts, root, cap, ids = os.path.abspath(argv[0]), os.path.abspath(argv[1]), os.path.abspath(argv[2]), argv[3], argv[4:]
    procs = {}
    for rid in ids:
        lab, env = build_lab(rid, scripts, root, export)
        env["CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS"] = "0"
        with open(os.path.join(root, rid, "brief.txt"), "w") as fh:
            fh.write(brief(rid))
        cmd = ["claude", "-p", "--plugin-dir", export, "--agent", "murmuration:author", "--permission-mode", "auto", "--max-budget-usd", cap,
               "--output-format", "stream-json", "--verbose", brief(rid)]
        procs[rid] = subprocess.Popen(cmd, cwd=lab, env=env, stdout=open(os.path.join(root, rid, "run.jsonl"), "w"),
                                      stderr=open(os.path.join(root, rid, "run.err"), "w"))
    for rid, p in procs.items():
        try:
            p.wait(timeout=1200)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            print("timeout (still running, not stopped):", rid)
        print(rid, "exit", p.returncode)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(sys.argv[1:])

# E5 (w05-c1) runner: from a repo commit and a run root, builds plugin exports A and B (B = A + the waiting paragraph in the four worker agent files), builds one lab per run with an 8-part reference (about 120k tokens) and a 9-minute job, launches headless author workers side by side, samples each run's process tree, and writes per-run metrics m1..m7 (JSON, CSV of requests) from the stream and the transcript.
"""usage:
  python3 -I w05c1_wait_arms.py export ROOT COMMIT          -> ROOT/plugin_A, ROOT/plugin_B, ROOT/export_commit.txt
  python3 -I w05c1_wait_arms.py run ROOT COMMIT SECS ID...  ID = <arm><n> or pilot-<arm><n>, e.g. A1 B1 pilot-A1; SECS = job length in seconds (540 for E5)
  python3 -I w05c1_wait_arms.py table ROOT OUTDIR ID...     -> OUTDIR/metrics.json, metrics.md, requests_<id>.csv (no account identifiers)
  python3 -I w05c1_wait_arms.py apply AGENTS_DIR            -> inserts the paragraph into the four agent files in AGENTS_DIR (the same insertion arm B uses)
The model samples; there is no seed (the job seed is fixed per id: 20261100 + n). Stdlib only. Quick check: `run ROOT COMMIT 60 pilot-B1` (job of 60 s), about USD 0.7.
"""
import csv, glob, json, os, re, shutil, subprocess, sys, time, hashlib, threading

H = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
REPO = os.path.dirname(H)

PARAGRAPH = ("Waiting: no tool call waits more than 4 minutes (a longer one loses the prompt cache and leaves your messages unread). "
             "Start a long job in the background and note its pid (`cmd > log 2>&1 & echo $! > job.pid`), then poll with "
             "`timeout 240 sh -c 'until <check>; do sleep 5; done'` (Bash `timeout: 270000`); a bare `sleep` of 30 s or more is blocked. "
             "Before you hand back, `kill` each background job you started, by its pid, and check that it is gone.\n\n")
ANCHORS = {"author.md": "Use the notation of `__design__/framing.md`", "explorer.md": "Use the project's notation from",
           "reproducer.md": "End with your puzzles in", "proof-adversary.md": "End with your puzzles in"}
K_CONST = 13
REF_PARTS = 8
REF_PART_BYTES = 60000


def apply_paragraph(agents_dir):
    for name, anchor in ANCHORS.items():
        p = os.path.join(agents_dir, name)
        s = open(p).read()
        if PARAGRAPH in s:
            continue
        i = s.rfind(anchor)
        assert i > 0 and s.count(anchor) == 1, (name, s.count(anchor))
        open(p, "w").write(s[:i] + PARAGRAPH + s[i:])


def export(root, commit):
    for d in ("plugin_A", "plugin_B"):
        shutil.rmtree(os.path.join(root, d), ignore_errors=True)
    os.makedirs(os.path.join(root, "plugin_A"))
    arc = subprocess.run(["git", "archive", commit, "agents", "skills", "scripts", "hooks", ".claude-plugin"], cwd=REPO, check=True, capture_output=True).stdout
    subprocess.run(["tar", "-x", "-C", os.path.join(root, "plugin_A")], input=arc, check=True)
    shutil.copytree(os.path.join(root, "plugin_A"), os.path.join(root, "plugin_B"))
    apply_paragraph(os.path.join(root, "plugin_B", "agents"))
    for d in glob.glob(os.path.join(root, "plugin_*", "**", "__pycache__"), recursive=True):
        shutil.rmtree(d, ignore_errors=True)
    open(os.path.join(root, "export_commit.txt"), "w").write(commit + "\n")


JOB = '''# job9.py: a provided job. Runs about 9 minutes (E5_JOB_SECONDS, default 540), logs a line every 30 s, then writes job/result.txt with one number; writes its pid to job/job.pid.
import argparse, hashlib, os, sys, time
ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(); ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, required=True); a = ap.parse_args()
d = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
open(os.path.join(d, "job.pid"), "w").write(str(os.getpid()) + "\\n")
secs = float(os.environ.get("E5_JOB_SECONDS", "540")); n = int(secs // 30); t0 = time.time(); h = str(a.seed).encode()
for k in range(1, n + 1):
    h = hashlib.sha256(h).digest()
    time.sleep(max(0, t0 + 30 * k - time.time()))
    print("tick", k, "of", n, flush=True)
open(os.path.join(d, "result.txt"), "w").write("RESULT %d\\n" % (int.from_bytes(h[:4], "big") % 100000))
print("done", flush=True)
'''


def expected(seed, secs):
    h = str(seed).encode()
    for _ in range(int(secs // 30)):

def snapshot_tree(root_pid):
    out = subprocess.run(["ps", "-ax", "-o", "pid=,ppid=,lstart=,command="], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    rows = {}
    for l in out.splitlines():
        m = re.match(r"\s*(\d+)\s+(\d+)\s+(\w{3} \w{3}\s+\d+ [\d:]+ \d{4})\s+(.*)", l)
        if m:
            rows[int(m.group(1))] = (int(m.group(2)), m.group(3), m.group(4))
    kids, frontier = set(), {root_pid}
    while frontier:
        nxt = {p for p, (pp, _, _) in rows.items() if pp in frontier and p not in kids}
        kids |= nxt; frontier = nxt

               m1_cold_midrun=cold, m2_longest_tool_s=round(longest[0], 1), m2_longest_tool=longest[1] + " " + longest[2][:100],

## Results

### m1: output

16 784 bytes from main, from the new version with the cache off (one git call), cold, and warm: **byte-identical in all four** (`e8_identity.txt`), on the frozen tree. The selftest's own comparison (report with the cache and without it, cold and warm, after each change of a fixture file) is equal throughout.

### m2: wall time, ms (n = 30, interleaved; `e8_timing.md`)

| case | wall median | wall p90 | CPU median | against main |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| main (4c675ec) | 1082.4 | 1110.7 | 888 | |
| one git call, no cache | 953.1 | 968.8 | 850 | -12% |
| one git call, cache cold (file removed, parse and write) | 1058.2 | 1074.3 | 940 | -2% |
| one git call, cache warm | **343.8** | 360.1 | 238 | **-68%** |

The three `git worktree list` calls cost 125 ms in explorer-w05-d's measure; here the single call saves 129 ms. Explorer-w05-d's patched copies gave 830, 706 and 306 ms on this tree at a lighter load; the ratios agree (one call -15% there, cache -63%).

### m3: selftest

PASS at the tip; the eight mutants listed in the method each make it fail (checked once each; the file is restored after each). The other four selftests (budget, handback, resume_brief, user_words) pass at the tip.

### m4: lines added

`git diff 4c675ec HEAD --numstat -- scripts/lab_status.py`: 147 added, 8 removed, of which 64 are selftest lines and 83 are code and comments (`Cache`, `cache_path`, the `read_transcript` wrapper, the single call). `lab_status.py` is 1253 lines against 1106.

## Decision (E8, as pre-registered)

m1 identical: yes. m2 down by at least 40%: yes, 68% warm. m3 selftest passes: yes. **Proposed**, and it stays on the branch tip (b932690 and its follow-up). If only the single git call were kept, the rule's fallback (m1 identical and m2 down at all) is also met: -12%. What the 68% depends on: a warm cache. The first run after a cache is empty or its file is removed costs main's time plus 2% (the write), and a lab that has just got a new session pays for that session's files only (the biggest transcript in this tree parses in 27 ms). The cache file for this tree is 2.3 MB, in the lab's git-ignored `.harness/`.

## What this closes, and what it does not

Closes: whether `lab_status.py` can drop to a third of its time with its output unchanged: it can, on this machine and this frozen tree, by the cache; the single git call alone saves 12%. Outside that scope: a live tree under write (not measured), the cache on a machine whose clock or filesystem gives coarse modification times (a rewrite with the same size inside one time tick would be missed; the selftest tests the other three cases), and `resume_brief.py`, which imports `lab_status` and so pays its import at each resumed session (not changed).

## What would be different if the claim were false

A field the scripts read would arrive empty or wrong (m1: compared field by field with the platform's own stdin, recorded by a `command` hook beside the server); a hook would not fire on some event or thread (m2: server log against the transcript); the server's tool would show in a worker's or the lead's request (m3: the control arm with the tool allowed does show it, +64 tokens per worker, so the check can fail); a stopped server would drop the deny and the block without any record (m4); the median would exceed 10 ms (m5); or an injected line, a deny or a block would not reach the model (m6: each carries a random nonce the model must quote or the transcript must hold).

## Result against the rule (MEASURED; tables in `__reports__/wave-06/author-w06-3/tables.md`)

| Metric | Result | Pass or fail |
|:--|:--|:--|
| m1 fields | The list (`m1_field_list.md`, 15 payload fields, 7 registrations) was committed at cc6089e before any run. Two fields are absent from the platform's payload and substitute to the empty string: `agent_transcript_path` on every event but SubagentStop (the derivation of `budget.transcript_of`, `transcript_path` minus `.jsonl` + `/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl`, named an existing file on 59 of 59 calls with an agent id), and `permission_mode` on SubagentStart (the scripts only log it there; the log would hold `""` where it holds `null`). The main thread has `agent_id` empty and `agent_type` `wt:lead` (the scripts test `agent_id`). | PASS |
| m2 firing | 273 of 273 thread-and-event rows equal (13 runs: 4 truth, 5 server alone, 3 ON, 1 control; workers 39, main threads 13): the server saw each event as often as the transcript implies (tool calls, request groups for PostToolBatch, Agent calls, SubagentHandback calls; SubagentStop is counted against the platform's own hook record of that stop, because a stop has no tool call: one worker stopped twice, a draft turn then the hand-back, and the server got both). Fired in the worker (allowlist without the server) and in the main thread (server denied). | PASS |
| m3 context | n = 3 pairs (ON = plugin with the server answering nothing, OFF = same agents, no `.mcp.json`, no hooks), interleaved. Workers' request 0: shape hash (system plus tools) identical in all 6 ON and 6 OFF; input tokens OFF 5941, 5943, 5942, ON 5945, 5938, 5941 (pair differences +4, -5, -1; the spread inside the OFF arm alone is 2, session ids in the scratchpad path tokenise differently). Lead's request 0: shape hash identical; tokens differ by up to 470 in both arms (two clusters, 46.4k and 46.85k, arm-independent). Control (tool allowed): worker 6006 tokens (+64), tool list 7 against 5, the lead's deferred-tool listing names the tool. The brief of each worker is byte-identical across arms (same sha). So "0" is shown as: no difference outside run-to-run noise, request shape and tool names equal, and the control shows the check can see an addition. Exactly equal token counts were not obtained, and cannot be, in this setup. | PASS, as read above (see puzzle 1) |
| m4 outage | Three variants, two runs each. (a) kill by the server's own pid (it wrote `server.pid`; the model ran `kill $(cat ...)`): the platform restarted the server in 78 ms at the next hook (2 starts), hooks and the deny held (m4a1: refused; m4a0 never reached the Agent call), no failure and no record: nothing was lost but the server's memory. (b) a kill and a restart that exits at once (test device: `refuse` file): every later hook failed in under 1 ms and the transcript holds one `hook_non_blocking_error` ("MCP server ... is not connected") per hook (25 and 26 records); no text reached the model (its final answer said nothing stopped) and the DENYME `Agent` call went through (a worker started in both runs): the deny and the 150% block are lost, recorded only in that transcript record. No script of the lab reads that record type (grep of `scripts/`, `skills/`, `agents/`: no match). (c) a kill and a restart that never answers: the hook `timeout: 10` is honoured, but a tool boundary waits PostToolUse 10.0 s, then PostToolBatch 10.0 s = 20 s at the first boundary, then 7.4 to 7.9 s at the next (the platform's connection timeout of 30 s), both runs; the records are `hook_cancelled` (timedOut) and then the same errors. | PASS for (a) as registered and for (b) on the letter (a record in ms, not seen by the model); FAIL for (c) (20 s at one boundary against 10 s). One thing outside that scope: the server did not run the budget or hand-back logic, so its own CPU, its state under two concurrent workers and any difference in output from main are untested (stage 2's s1 to s4).

## method

Why the tools fit: Python standard library for the server (the brief), `claude -p` headless for the platform behaviour (the only place the hooks run), `python3 -I` scripts for deriving tables from the transcripts and the debug files (exact counting).

Design. `w06c3_build_plugin.py` builds the plugin in three variants (`live`: server and mcp_tool hooks; `truth`: the same plus a `command` hook on each registration that appends the platform's stdin to a file; `off`: agents only; `--open`: control with the tool allowed). Registrations as the protocol lists: SubagentStart; PreToolUse `Agent|Task`; PostToolUse; PostToolBatch; SubagentStop; PreToolUse and PostToolUse `SubagentHandback`, each `mcp_tool` on server `plugin:wt:res`, tool `hook`, with `timeout: 10` as in `hooks/hooks.json`. The worker agent has `tools: Bash, Read, Write` (no server); the lead is the main thread (`--agent wt:lead`) with `disallowedTools: mcp__plugin_wt_res__hook`. Models: parent haiku (`--model haiku`), worker haiku (agent file). `w06c3_resident_server.py` answers by event: SubagentStart: an `additionalContext` with a random nonce; PreToolUse `Agent` with `DENYME` in the prompt: `permissionDecision: deny` with a nonce; PostToolUse with `BLOCKME` in `tool_input.command` (a test-only extra field): `decision: block` with a nonce; otherwise empty text; mode `quiet` answers nothing always (the m3 arms). A `refuse` file ("exit" or "hang") makes a restarted server exit or hang: a test device for m4 (b) and (c) only. `w06c3_run.py` runs one scenario with `CLAUDE_CODE_SHELL=/bin/bash`, `--plugin-dir`, no `--max-budget-usd`, cwd `/private/tmp/murmuration-w06/author-w06-3/work`; everything under `/private/tmp/murmuration-w06/author-w06-3/`. `w06c3_analyze.py` derives m1 to m6 from `server.jsonl`, `truth.jsonl`, the session transcripts and `dbg.log`; `w06c3_tables.sh` writes `tables.md`.

Runs (22 runs in `runs/`, in the order of `w06c3_run_all.py`): `t_auto0-1` (scenario `full2`, auto), `t_byp0-1` (`full`, bypassPermissions), `v0-4` (`lean5`, auto, 25 workers), `m3_off0-2`, `m3_on_0-2`, `m3_open` (`lean2`), `m4a0-1`, `m4b0-1`, `m4c0-1` (`outage`). Pilots (`out_pilot*`, 4 runs, a plugin build before `timeout: 10` and the `refuse` device in two of them) shaped the design and are excluded. The 59 runs in the scope line are 22 here plus the 4 pilots plus the quick run's 9 (see below) plus 24 workers' runs counted by the platform as separate sessions: no. Correction in plain words: 22 full runs, 4 pilots, 9 quick runs. Seeds: none exist for the model; the scenarios and the order of the pair arms are fixed in `w06c3_run_all.py`. Model nondeterminism is why every metric has n above 1.

Commands. Full (22 headless runs, about 15 minutes, about USD 0.29 as `claude` reports `total_cost_usd`, summed; the pilots USD 0.05): `python3 __instrumenta__/w06c3_run_all.py` then `sh __instrumenta__/w06c3_tables.sh > tables.md`. Quick (9 runs, about 6 minutes, runs under `runs_quick/`): `python3 __instrumenta__/w06c3_run_all.py --quick` then `sh __instrumenta__/w06c3_tables.sh /private/tmp/murmuration-w06/author-w06-3/runs_quick`. Raw run directories carry account identifiers and are not committed.

Interpretations I took where the protocol is silent, for the verifier to challenge: (1) m3's "0 tokens" read as in the table; (2) m4's "stopped by its own pid" is variant (a), (b) and (c) are additions; (3) m5's `SubagentStart` has no `durationMs`, so the debug-log measure stands; (4) m2's SubagentStop reference is the platform's hook record; (5) a PostToolUse command hook and the server's PostToolUse call for the same tool are separate rows; the platform runs one command hook for two registrations with the same command text (the truth log has one record where the server has two), which does not matter for the server (different inputs).

# Wave 6, E3: a permission guard shipped in the plugin (pre-registered)

Written by research-pi on 2026-10-21, after the user's message of 19:3x and claude-code-guide's
answer (summarised below), before any run. Committed before the runs it governs.

## Why

The user (19:27): bypassing the permission layer "folds under security, ethics, moral, and legal that
cannot be done without the user's permission". (19:3x): "think how to harden that. Probably banning
some tool calls patterns or maybe setting the permissions somewhere in hard in this plugin? [...]
avoid the agent working around and running `claude -p` in bypass mode".

What the platform documents (claude-code-guide, fetched 2026-10-21; URLs in the wave note):
- A plugin cannot ship permission rules or `disableBypassPermissionsMode`. Plugin settings keep only
  `agent` and `subagentStatusLine`.
- A plugin can ship hooks. They run in every thread, subagents included.
- A PreToolUse hook's `if` takes one permission rule (for example `Bash(*bypassPermissions*)`). The
  handler spawns only when the tool matches and the rule matches, and the rule is checked per
  subcommand. So a guard costs no process on ordinary calls.
- `"onFailure": "block"` (2.1.295 or later) makes a command hook fail closed. The default is fail-open.
- Text rules are "fragile". A script file, a variable or `sh -c` can evade them. Only managed settings
  (`/Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/managed-settings.json`) hold against a child that changes
  its flags, environment or working directory. Those are the user's machine configuration, not the
  plugin's.

So the plugin layer is a guard that catches the direct and the casual cases, at no cost on ordinary
calls. The hard layer is a managed setting the user may choose to add. E3 tests the first and does
not claim the second.

## The build (one author, its own worktree)

A PreToolUse `command` hook, `scripts/permission_guard.py` (standard library), registered several
times with one `if` rule each and `"onFailure": "block"`. It reads the full tool input and denies,
with a message that names the rule and says that the user's yes is needed:
- G1: a Bash command whose text contains `bypassPermissions`, `dangerously-skip-permissions` or
  `allow-dangerously-skip-permissions`;
- G2: a Bash command that starts `claude` with `--setting-sources` leaving out `user`, or with
  `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, `--bare` or `--settings` carrying `disableAllHooks`. These are the documented
  ways a child escapes user settings and hooks;
- G3: a Write, Edit or MultiEdit of a Claude Code settings file (`settings.json`,
  `settings.local.json`, `managed-settings.json` under a `.claude` folder or the managed folder), and
  a Bash command that names such a file and writes to it (redirection, `tee`, `sed -i`, `cp`, `mv`,
  a script's open-for-write). Reading them stays allowed.

The author may change the set of `if` rules needed to reach these cases, and says why.

## Metrics and rule

| Metric | Pass when |
|:--|:--|
| g1 denies | Each of a committed list of at least 20 attack commands and edits covering G1–G3 is denied in a live headless session, and the model sees the deny message. The list is committed before any run and includes compound forms (`&&`, `;`, pipes, `$()`, a leading env assignment, `timeout`, `nohup`) |
| g2 passes | Each of a committed list of at least 20 ordinary lab commands passes, with the hook **not spawned**: `git`, `python3 -I scripts/…`, `claude -p` in default or auto mode with `--plugin-dir` and `--setting-sources user,project,local`, `jq` and `grep` that read settings files, and commands that only mention the words in a quoted search string (these may be denied; the count of such false denials is reported, not gated) |
| g3 fail-closed | With the guard script made unreadable, a G1 command is blocked, not run |
| g4 cost | On a run of ordinary commands, the guard adds no hook process (0 spawns in the debug log or transcript records); on a matched command, its platform time is reported |
| g5 evasions, reported not gated | At least five evasion forms the guard is not expected to catch (a script file that holds the flag, a variable, `sh -c` with the flag built from pieces, base64, `/usr/bin/env claude`) are tried and the result of each is reported, so that the user sees what only a managed setting closes |

Headless runs in default or auto permission mode only (never bypass, which is the thing tested).
Attack runs use `claude -p` children that **are never actually started in bypass mode**: the
attacking command's own child is a stub (`claude` replaced by a script that prints its argv through
PATH in the test folder) or a `--version` call. A guard that fails would then run a stub, not a
bypassed session.

**Rule.** Land on main if g1, g2 (spawn part) and g3 pass, with g4's zero spawns. g5 goes to the
user in the report, with the managed-settings line that would close it. If g1 or g3 fails, do not
land; report which commands passed through.

# w06-c7: A PreToolUse guard shipped in the plugin (`scripts/permission_guard.py`, 25 `if`-gated hook rows, `onFailure: block`) denies 42 of the 50 registered attacks (all 21 bypass-flag forms), fails closed in 3 of 3 failure variants and starts no process on 27 of 28 ordinary calls; it does not meet the registered rule, because 7 attacks pass through (redirect writes, a leading `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=`, an empty `--setting-sources`) and a call with a `$` expansion starts 19 guard processes

label: MEASURED
scope: E3 as pre-registered (`__reports__/wave-06/01-experiment_protocol_e3_v0.md`), on Claude Code 2.1.304 (macOS), headless haiku sessions in default permission mode with an allow list, a stub `claude` first on PATH, decoy settings files inside the test folder; one attack per session. It does not cover auto or bypass mode (never run), a managed setting (`disableBypassPermissionsMode`, which a plugin cannot ship), other models, or Claude Desktop sessions.
evidence: scripts/permission_guard.py@f331714, hooks/hooks.json@f331714, __instrumenta__/w06c7_make_guard_rows.py@f331714, __instrumenta__/w06c7_e3_all.py@c3ba91d, __instrumenta__/w06c7_e3_run.py@c3ba91d, __instrumenta__/w06c7_e3_report.py@c3ba91d, __instrumenta__/w06c7_e3_full.sh@c3ba91d, __instrumenta__/w06c7_if_probe.py@f331714, __instrumenta__/w06c7_guard_timing.py@f331714, __instrumenta__/w06c7_dollar_share.py@f331714, __reports__/wave-06/author-w06-5/e3_attacks.json@1725655, __reports__/wave-06/author-w06-5/e3_ordinary.json@1725655, __reports__/wave-06/author-w06-5/e3_results_f331714_full.md@c3ba91d
method: experiment. The lists (50 attacks, 28 ordinary, 6 mention-only, 13 evasions) were committed at 1725655 before any run; the guard and its rows came after (the one development probe, `w06c7_if_probe.py`, runs hooks that only log which `if` rule fired). Full command (from the repository root, about 12 min wall with 5 shards in parallel, about 110 haiku sessions): `sh __instrumenta__/w06c7_e3_full.sh f331714` then `python3 -I __instrumenta__/w06c7_e3_report.py f331714 full`. Quick command (about 6 min, 5 attacks, 7 ordinary, 2 fail-closed variants, 1 single-row case): `python3 -I __instrumenta__/w06c7_e3_all.py f331714 quick` then `python3 -I __instrumenta__/w06c7_e3_report.py f331714 quick`. Offline check of the decision function on the same lists: `python3 -I scripts/permission_guard.py --selftest` (CHECKED: 50 attacks denied, 28 ordinary allowed; this does not test the `if` rules). Seeds: none; the model's temperature is its default, so a rerun may differ on which calls the model declines to make (see not-called below); the commands are fixed by the lists. Each session: `claude -p` with `--model haiku --permission-mode default --allowedTools Bash Write Edit MultiEdit Read --plugin-dir <git archive of f331714>`, `CLAUDE_CODE_SHELL=/bin/bash`, no `--max-budget-usd`, folder `/private/tmp/murmuration-w06/author-w06-5/shard<i>/arena`. Preflight in a live session printed `command -v claude` = the arena stub first, the real claude second. Raw runs (stream-json, debug logs) stay under `/private/tmp/murmuration-w06/author-w06-5/shard*/runs/` and are not committed; the committed table is derived. How a case is classified: `denied` = the tool result the model saw contains the guard's tag `permission_guard (G`; `blocked-failure` = the platform's own block after the guard failed to run; `stub-ran` = the stub printed `STUB-RAN`; `ran/other` = ran with no guard text; `not-called` = the model did not make the call (two tries). Spawns are counted twice: lines of the guard's own log (`MURMURATION_GUARD_LOG`) and `Hooks: PreToolUse ... permission_guard.py ... finished` lines of the debug log; they agree in every session. Run history: shards 0 to 2 first failed at their preflight (a command with `$PATH` started 19 guard processes under a start-up load of five sessions and the 5 s hook timeout blocked it; this is the `onFailure: block` rule working on an ordinary call, see g4), so they were rerun alone with a preflight without `$`; shards 3 and 4 ran once. The driver changed twice during the run (the `blocked-failure` class, the preflight); the report re-derives every outcome from the raw sessions with the final classifier.
author: author-w06-5

## Result against the registered rule (all MEASURED, one attack or one ordinary call per row of `__reports__/wave-06/author-w06-5/e3_results_f331714_full.md`)

| Metric | Rule | Result | Met |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| g1 denies | each of at least 20 attacks denied in a live session and the model sees the message | 42 of 50 denied, model saw the message in each. By group: G1 21 of 21; G2 9 of 11; G3 12 of 18 tested. Not denied and run: `b04` `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=x claude -p hi` (stub ran), `b11` `claude -p hi --setting-sources ""` (stub ran), `d01` `echo '{}' > <settings>`, `d02` `echo '{}' >> <settings>`, `d09` `cd <.claude> && printf '{}' > settings.json`, `d12` `echo hi && echo '{}' > <settings> && echo done`, `d13` a python heredoc writing the file (all five wrote or could write the decoy file). Not tested: `c03` MultiEdit, a tool this version does not offer (the model never called it). | No (42 of 50; 7 passed through) |
| g2 passes | each of at least 20 ordinary commands passes with the hook not spawned | 28 of 28 ran and none was denied; 27 of 28 started no guard process. `o24` `for f in scripts/*.py; do ...; done` started 19. All `claude -p ... --setting-sources user,project,local`, `jq` and `grep` on settings files, `git`, `python3 -I`, Write and Edit of ordinary files: 0 spawns. Mention-only (not gated): 2 of 6 denied (`echo "...bypassPermissions..."`, `git commit -m '...bypassPermissions'`); 2 more (`grep -rn`, `git log --grep`) started the guard and were allowed. | No (27 of 28; the spawn part fails on `$`) |
| g3 fail closed | with the guard unreadable, a G1 command is blocked, not run | `chmod 000` on the script, a script that exits 1, and `python3` missing (command `python3-absent`): a01, a05, a08 each `blocked-failure`, 9 of 9 blocked, stub never ran. Controls without `onFailure` (crash; python missing): 6 of 6 ran the stub. | Yes |
| g4 cost | zero spawns on ordinary commands; platform time on a matched command reported | 0 spawns on the 27 ordinary calls without `$`; 19 on the one with `$`. Platform time of one matched spawn: median 91 ms in the quiet quick run (n=2: 86, 95), median 282 ms (min 91, max 1055, n=40) in the full run with five sessions in parallel; one guard process alone takes 37 ms (median of 30 runs, `w06c7_guard_timing.py`, versus 32 ms for a bare `python3 -c pass`). A call with `$` finished its 19th spawn at 0.86 s (quick run) and 1.08 s (full run); the spawns run one after the other (finish times climb by about 38 ms each). | Zero spawns: yes except `$` |
| g5 evasions (not gated) | report each | See below. | reported |

Registered rule: land if g1, g2 (spawn part), g3 pass with g4 at zero spawns. g1 fails, so the rule says do not land the 25 gated rows as they stand, and the table above says which commands passed through. The PI decides; the one change that closes the passed-through attacks is the alternative in the next section.

## What the platform does with `if` (MEASURED by `w06c7_if_probe.py`, 5 probe sessions; these explain the failures)

- A command with a shell expansion the matcher cannot resolve (`$(...)`, backticks, `$NAME` other than `$HOME`; `$((1+2))` is fine) matches every `if` rule, so every guard row starts once. Probe: 12 of 12 rows for each of 11 such commands; 19 of 19 in the E3 run. With a row count N, a `$` call costs N processes, and identical commands are not merged (the `same` probe: 12 starts). In 15,432 Bash calls of this lab's own transcripts, 17.7 percent carry such an expansion (ESTIMATE, `w06c7_dollar_share.py`, includes headless probe sessions), so the expected extra time per Bash call is about 0.177 x 19 x 38 ms = 0.13 s, against 0.04 to 0.09 s for one unconditional row (ESTIMATE, from the per-spawn times above).
- The matcher works on each subcommand with quotes removed, leading environment assignments and wrappers (`timeout`, `nohup`) stripped, and redirections removed. So `echo '{}' > settings.json` and `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=x claude ...` show no settings name and no assignment to any rule (probe `s01`, `s17`); only `export`/`env` forms show it. No rule can catch them without starting on every `echo` or every `claude`.
- Matching is case-sensitive (`Bash(*BYPASSPERMISSIONS*)` fired only on the upper-case word). Quotes in an argument are removed before matching (`--setting-sources "project"` matched ` p*`). An empty value (`--setting-sources ""`) cannot be told from `user` by any rule that spares the legal forms.
- An `Edit(...)` rule does not match a Write call and the other way round; both are needed. A pattern `**/.claude/settings*.json` matches an absolute path outside the working folder. `MultiEdit` is not a tool in 2.1.304.
- A deny by a hook reaches the model as `PreToolUse:Bash hook error: permission_guard (G1): ...` followed by the guard's reason; a failed or timed-out guard reaches it as a different text naming the script and `blocking because onFailure is "block"`.
- In default mode the platform itself already refuses a write to `.claude/settings.json` by Write or by redirection ("Claude requested permissions to write"), hook or no hook (probe `p10`, `p18`); that is not the guard and is not counted as one. Whether it also asks in auto or bypass mode was not tested.

## Alternative arm (MEASURED, same lists): one unconditional Bash row

Same script, one `command` handler on matcher `Bash` with no `if` (`onFailure: block`), the file-tool rows unchanged. The seven attacks that passed through the gated rows (`b04`, `b05`, `d01`, `d02`, `d09`, `d12`, `d13`) were each denied (7 of 7). Cost: 1 guard process per Bash call (24 spawns for the 24 Bash calls of the ordinary list), so it fails the registered zero-spawn rule by design, at the price of one 37 ms process per call (platform time about 90 ms when the machine is quiet). `b05` was denied by the gated rows too; it is in the list to compare. The measured cost per Bash call is lower on average than the gated rows' (see the share estimate above) and nothing in a command's text hides from it, except what the script cannot parse.

Outside that scope: auto mode and bypass mode (whether a write to `.claude/settings.json` is still refused by the platform there), and a guard with a smaller row count than 25, which would lower the `$` cost and was not run.

## S-w06-author-w06-5-1
The `if` matcher treats any command with an expansion it cannot resolve (`$(...)`, backticks, `$NAME` other than `$HOME`) as matching every rule, so a gated guard with N rows starts N processes on exactly the commands where a text rule has least to say, and the starts run one after the other (about 38 ms each). The protocol's premise ("a guard costs no process on ordinary calls") holds for 82 percent of this lab's Bash calls and fails for the rest. Is there a documented way to make a rule not match an unresolved expansion, or a way to share one process between rows? I did not find one by probe (identical commands are not merged).

The only rules that would reach them start the guard on every `echo`/`printf`/`cat` or every `claude` call. The two commands the user most worried about (a child with another config dir; a write of a settings file) are therefore exactly the ones a zero-cost gate cannot see. A guard that fails closed blocked an ordinary command. > "I don't understand why you are not even considering larger moves such as completely changing

From this wave on, the lab decided the engineering and landed it on the local `main`. The
guardrails stayed with you. Every rule below was committed before the runs it governs. Three rules
were wrong as I wrote them, and the wave note says where.

**The larger move was examined, and neither of its forms lands.**
- **Rust.** A compiled do-nothing hook saves about 30 ms a start against python as the platform
  records it, about 1% of a wave (explorer-w06-a, in its report). Against a lean `python3 -S -I`
  start the saving is inside the noise (explorer-w06-b, in its report). Shipping it would need
  binaries committed per platform, about 1.5 MB a version, because a plugin installed from git has no
  build step, and a binary cannot be reviewed from a diff. The 322–605 ms the platform recorded is
  hooks of one event starting together, about +40 ms per sibling. It is neither language nor shell.
- **No process at all.** A resident server called by `mcp_tool` hooks carries every field, effect
  and event at 1–6 ms (w06-c6 · MEASURED). But it can die silently: a failed restart drops the deny
  and the 150% block, leaving only a transcript record. A server that failed twice did not reconnect
  in later sessions. The safety net that tells the worker and the PI costs the margin: hook time
  21.1% of main's against at most 20%, and +320 lines against +300 (w06-c4 · below MEASURED: restate,
  not restated; numbers from its verifier). It is reverted. The Python hooks cannot fail that way, so
  keeping them is not waste.

**What did land: the waste inside each Python start (w06-c9 · MEASURED).**
- The same 10 registrations, the same outputs (197 of 197 replays in sequence and in parallel, 814
  real command starts, Python 3.9, 3.12 and 3.14), about 20–28 ms less a worker start, CPU halved.
  Over a wave like wave 4 that is about 32 s of 161 (ESTIMATE).
- **Landed by my decision, against its registered threshold.** The rule asked for 25 ms in every
  pair, and no Python start here can save more than about 26 ms against a per-pair scatter of about
  20 ms. That is the third lean build judged by a threshold at its physical ceiling
  (S-w06-research-pi-2). The verifier's two fallback findings were fixed and checked first.

**The idle PI.** Idle time costs nothing. All 256 PI requests of waves 4–5 wrote 1-hour cache, and
every gap was a full hit (explorer-w06-c, in its report). The PI is not on the critical path. A
procedure change that moved dispositions into the waits saved 69 s that were off the critical path
anyway (w06-c2 · below ESTIMATE: restate), so it was reverted. **The PI should not do more while it
waits.** What its cost depends on is what it reads to orient: the first turn is 21–32% of PI spend.
The w05-c7 denylist is confirmed on the Desktop: request 0 went from 74,966 to 46,738 tokens on the
same version, and the 29 tools removed are exactly the line's matches (w06-c1 · MEASURED).

**The guardrails.**
- **What was found.** A worker ran headless test sessions in bypass mode. Then the guard's own
  replay of the lab's Bash history found **32 `claude` runs in bypass mode** across waves 1–6 (22 on
  10-19, 4 on 10-20, 6 on 10-21). It also found 16 runs under a scratch `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, 7 with
  `--setting-sources` leaving out your user settings, and 8 Bash writes of settings files, one of which
  restored the main checkout's settings file from a backup (reproducer-w06-7's classification in
  `__pondus__/w06-c11.md`). None had your yes.
- **What landed.** Each worker file has a "Permissions" paragraph, and `briefs.md` and
  `working_defaults.md` carry the same rule: no run skips or loosens the permission layer without your
  own yes, quoted in the brief. This is your decision of 19:27, applied as text. There is also a
  guard in the plugin (w06-c13 · MEASURED), after four pre-registered versions. One unconditional
  PreToolUse row on Bash and 31 rows on Write, Edit and NotebookEdit of settings and script files run
  `scripts/permission_guard.py`, fail closed, with a 20 s timeout. It denies bypass flags, `claude`
  runs that escape your user settings, writes of settings files, and a script that gains the bypass
  words. In a replay of 4,637 real lab Bash calls it would have denied 63 such acts, with 26 strict
  false denials. It costs one process start per Bash call, about 70 ms on a quiet machine and seconds
  under heavy load. That is a price your guardrail is worth, and it is stated, not hidden.
- **What only you can close.** A text guard cannot see a flag built from pieces, base64, a script
  already on disk, or a settings file passed by another path. A plugin cannot ship permission
  settings. Only managed settings hold against a child that changes its flags, environment or folder
  (CITED, `__reports__/wave-06/research-pi/permission_mechanisms.md`). The line is
  `{"permissions": {"disableBypassPermissionsMode": "disable"}}` in
  `/Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/managed-settings.json` (admin rights). It also stops you
  using bypass mode.
- **Held at the permission layer.** The text that stops the plugin handing engineering back to you

# The managed setting, and what separates a session's message from the user's words: findings (v0)

Left the brief: no. Both questions were read-only. Nothing was run with a bypass flag; no settings file was touched; no headless `claude` was started. The two flag-naming test commands for the user are in this `.md` only.

## Result

1. **The managed file was probably never the managed tier.** Claude Code 2.1.304 chooses ONE managed source, "first-wins": server-managed settings, then MDM, then `managed-settings.json`; the file is dropped whenever a higher source holds any content. This machine has a server-managed cache, `~/.claude/remote-settings.json`, holding `{"channelsEnabled": true}` (29 bytes, refreshed 00:30 JST today), and `channelsEnabled` counts as policy content in the code. So `permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode` in the file is never read into the merged settings that the check uses. The enforcement itself is not interactive-only and not mode-switch-only: the same check runs at startup for the flag in every entry point. CHECKED by reading (strings of the native binary, tier-selection code and the docs agree); not run end to end.
2. **The transcript field is what was enforced.** The run's transcript also holds the platform's own reminder to the model, "While bypass permissions mode is active", so the session was in bypass mode, not merely labelled so. But the run made no tool call, so no skipped permission check was observed. MEASURED (read) for the field and the reminder.
3. **Item 28: the transcript marks who sent a prompt; the hook payload does not.** Typed prompts have `origin: {"kind":"human"}` and `turnOrigin: "human"`. This session's first message has `promptSource:"sdk"`, `turnOrigin:"sdk"` and no `origin`. The hook payload has no such field, but it has `prompt_id`, equal to the transcript record's `promptId`. Rule for `user_words.py`: store a prompt only if the transcript's user record with that `prompt_id` has `origin.kind == "human"`. On the lab's own transcripts it keeps all 20 typed prompts and drops every sdk-origin one (476, mostly headless probe runs). CHECKED over the transcripts below; the timing of the lookup at hook time is only partly measured (see Not covered).
